summary:
Wide lens is an interactive, browser-based astronomical viewer designed to make time-domain FITS imagery from the SPHEREx mission fast, accessible, and easy to analyze.
Raw astronomical archives are often heavy and require specialized desktop software to inspect. Wide lens solves this challenge by pairing a Python Astropy backend—which dynamically fetches and trims custom sky cutouts (Cutout2D) from NASA IRSA archives—with an Aladin Lite v3 WebGL frontend. Users can enter any celestial coordinates (RA/Dec), animate multi-epoch observations via a built-in time-lapse player, adjust real-time histogram stretching and colormaps, and overlay independent multi-mission data (WISE, 2MASS, DSS2, GALEX).
By combining rapid multi-wavelength comparison with an automated FITS metadata and contamination flag inspector, Wide lens accelerates the discovery of moving objects, brown dwarfs, and variable stars without local setup overhead.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Wide lens bridges raw space-telescope archives and rapid visual discovery directly in a web browser:
Dynamic Sky Cutouts (Cutout2D): When a user enters coordinates (RA/Dec) or selects a preset astronomical target, the Astropy backend queries NASA/Caltech IRSA archives, crops the massive raw FITS files to the requested field of view (10' to 2°) while preserving exact World Coordinate System (WCS) headers, and streams lightweight FITS files to the client.
Temporal Time-Lapse Engine: The frontend caches rendered WebGL FITS layers in memory, enabling smooth, zero-latency playback across different observation dates with adjustable frame rates (FPS) and timeline scrubbing.
Real-Time WebGL Histogram Controls: Users can dynamically switch stretch functions (Asinh, Log, Sqrt, Linear), fine-tune non-linear Min/Max Cut thresholds, and apply scientific colormaps (Grayscale, Viridis, Inferno, Rainbow) directly on the GPU.
Independent Multi-Mission Overlay: A dedicated secondary pipeline allows users to superimpose and animate data from complementary missions (WISE, 2MASS, DSS2, GALEX) with independent coordinates, cutout sizes, colormaps, and 0–100% opacity blending.
Metadata & Quality Inspector: A slide-out drawer parses FITS headers, automatically detects the source mission, and highlights quality/contamination flags.
Benefits & Intended Impact
Full-frame SPHEREx FITS files are massive and slow to download. By performing server-side Cutout2D extraction and client-side WebGL caching, Wide lens reduces load times from minutes to seconds. This lowers the technical barrier for researchers, students, and citizen scientists to verify transient events, spot proper-motion objects (like fast brown dwarfs), and cross-check anomalies across wavelengths.
Tools, Languages & Technologies Used
Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Aladin Lite v3 (WebGL & WebAssembly FITS rendering).
Backend: Python, Astropy (astropy.io.fits, astropy.wcs, astropy.nddata.Cutout2D), PyVO / Requests (NASA IRSA archive queries).
Creativity & Key Design Considerations
Dual-Timeline Architecture: Instead of static overlays, we engineered two independent time-lapse engines—allowing users to scrub through historical WISE epochs on top of a fixed SPHEREx frame (or vice versa) to visually detect motion and variability.
Performance & Clean Execution: We implemented client-side layer caching for instant frame switching and intercepted redundant external HiPS/survey requests so the app runs cleanly and deterministically on custom backend data.
Data Reliability: We prioritized scientific integrity by preserving WCS headers during cropping and surfacing raw FITS metadata and contamination flags in a non-intrusive drawer so users always know the exact provenance and quality of every pixel.
